newsitem.title: IRELAND: GOLF-BALLESTEROS GIVES UP HOPE OF BEING PLAYING CAPTAIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BALLESTEROS GIVES UP HOPE OF BEING PLAYING CAPTAIN.

text.p: Seve Ballesteros finally conceded on Thursday that he was highly unlikely to be a playing captain of Europe's Ryder Cup team against the Americans at Valderrama in September.

"I'm not going to play at Valderrama. The way I'm playing it would not be fair to pick myself - unless things change dramatically," he said after struggling to a four-over-par 75 in the first round of the Irish Open.
Ballesteros had maintained right up to this week that he would not be rule out being Europe's first playing captain until the squad was chosen after August 31.
But after putting himself in danger of missing his ninth cut in 11 starts this year, while suffering further from a recurring back injury, he said he was "ready to throw in the towel."
"It seems to me it's not possible to play and be the captain, and do a good job. So unless there's a miracle, I'll not be playing in the team, just being a good captain, I hope.
"It's been difficult because I've been struggling for a long time with my back as well as my game and things have not gone well.
"I don't want to keep talking about the back problems but obviously they have not helped me."
His predecessor in the European captain's chair, Bernard Gallacher, had urged Ballesteros strongly last month not to think about trying to play.

"Seve should not consider being playing captain even if he wins the British Open," said Gallacher, who led Europe to victory at Oak Hill in 1995, "because he cannot possibly organise the pairings if he is out on the course."
